points.response: Conceded only in part — RD-3(a) exempts the *point* named (Paya Lebar Square), not a 4.57 km loop that strayed up to 729 m off the optimal corridor (F4), and the rider's own messages name only a stop of '3-4 minutes' (F9, F10), so D1 is at most a bar to referee that a Paya Lebar Square stop was permitted, not a defence to the extra 2.97 km.

Accept that the disputed item is the single off-route segment (F4), not the whole fare — but that segment is precisely the unexempted extra distance, and it is the basis of this claim, not a reason to deny it.

The driver's own arithmetic shows the refund basis: 2.97 km extra on the unexempted segment multiplied by the same $1.4100/km rate the driver cites equals $4.19 (2.97 × 1.41 = 4.1877, rounded to $4.19), versus the driver's $4.91, which charged the rider for 3.48 km of unadjudicated mileage; RD-2 refunds the unexempted segment's extra_km, and the difference to the full $4.91 is the corridor/rounding mileage RD-2 expressly does not refund (F4, F5, F8).
Concede — the rider does not seek the $1.15 of metered waiting time (F6), which is chargeable on a RydeTAXI trip under RD-3(c), and this was already stated in my brief (C7).

Agreed: with no incident on the route (F15) and only mid-range bands on the PIE and CTE (F13, F14) in fair weather (F16), no RD-4 exemption applies to the unexempted segment, which is exactly why it is refundable under RD-2.
Conceded — the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days (F18), so no flag_account request is made and RD-6 is not in play.

The +3.5 km / +22% figure (F1) is an aggregate of the whole trip, not a billing finding; the fare facts show the billed distance was 18.95 km, i.e. only 3.48 km above optimal, and the billed excess is $4.91 (F5, F8), so C1's non-metered 'route whose optimal length is 15.5 km' framing overstates the recoverable amount.

We do not contest that the 12:25–12:36 stretch added 2.97 km (F4); our point is only that the rider herself directed the stop that the segment served (F9), so the excess must be measured as the segment's extra_km under RD-2 rather than as the full 4.57 km driven.

Correct that a stop request is not consent to a routing change: under RD-3(b) the rider named Paya Lebar Square, and nothing in the record ties the driven segment to any named road she agreed to (F9, F11, F12), so the excess distance within that segment is not exempt.

The 4 min 0 s stationary period at 12:28–12:32 is 5890 m from pickup and 4243 m from drop-off (F2), which is the Paya Lebar Square parcel stop the rider requested (F9), so it corroborates a genuine errand stop but does not convert the segment's excess distance into exempt mileage.

Conceded: with no incidents near the route (F15) and only band 5 on the PIE and band 4 on the CTE in fair weather (F13, F14, F16), the driver has no RD-4 reasonable-cause exemption for the extra distance, and our brief already declines to claim one.

Their $4.19 figure is a narrower request than the $4.91 the fare facts support: RD-2 sets the refund as Σ(unexempted extra_km) × (distance fare ÷ distance km), and the billed excess-distance line is 3.48 km × $1.4100/km = $4.91 (F5, F8), whereas $4.19 rests solely on rounding the single segment's 2.97 km (F4); either way the amount is computable from the fare table, so the driver does not oppose a refund in the $4.19–$4.91 range.
Agreed and unchallenged: the $1.15 waiting charge is metered waiting time (4.4 min × $0.26/min) during the rider's own named stop and is not refundable (F6, F9).

The driver's post-trip statement (F12) cannot widen the rider's consent: under G11 a driver's assertion of a verbal arrangement is a claim, not consent, and RD-5 requires the rider's own pre-segment message, which here covered only a stop at Paya Lebar Square (F9, F11).

We do not seek and do not oppose the absence of a flag_account: with 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days and no repeated-violation record (F18), RD-6's predicate is not met and no account action should attach.

notices.text: We have reviewed your dispute: part of the fare is refunded. You will receive $4.19 as a Ryde voucher. The decision follows Ryde's dispute policy and the trip record.

We reviewed a fare dispute on this trip. The outcome: no change to your account and no action against you. The rider's request to stop at Paya Lebar Square, which you accepted and made, means the drive to that stop isn't treated as a detour. However, part of that stretch still measured as extra distance with no route change agreed in the chat beforehand, so $4.19 of the fare is refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. The waiting time and the rest of the metered fare are unchanged, and the fare adjustment is not a finding against you.
